exposure: mode of delivery (operative, spontaneous vaginal, elective C-section, emergency C-section)
cohort: 139 pregnant women who delivered a live baby at term, excluding those with a history of assisted reproductive techniques, diagnosed mental or chronic medical illness, or antenatally diagnosed fetal anomaly.
finding: Postnatal depression was observed in 21.58% of patients overall, with a significantly higher frequency (76.6%) in women who underwent emergency caesarean section compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery (6.67%) or elective C-section (6.3%).
mod_finding: Postnatal depression is more frequent in women who underwent emergency caesarean section compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery or elective C-section.
